content: Visit note | 2025-01-05 02:00 PM | Dr. Saiful Alam, Endocrinology | Patient: Rashed Uddin, 70, male. Mr. Uddin attends today because he has been feeling cold all the time, even in warm weather, and has noticed that his clothes have become tighter over the past few months. He works as a shopkeeper and spends long days standing behind the counter of his small grocery shop. The change was first pointed out by colleagues in Dhanmondi, who remarked that he seemed to have gained weight around the face and waist. He says he has not changed his eating habits and has not been eating more than usual. He also mentions feeling slower than before, with less energy for his daily work, and he has been sleeping longer but still waking unrefreshed. He has Essential hypertension, for which he takes his medicines regularly, and he reports no missed doses. He denies chest pain, palpitations, or breathlessness on walking. He denies any neck swelling, difficulty swallowing, or hoarseness of voice. He also denies constipation and reports that his bowel habit is unchanged. On examination, he is alert and oriented, with a puffy face and dry, coarse skin. His voice is slightly hoarse. The thyroid gland is not visibly enlarged and no nodule is felt. On examination: TSH 17.8 mIU/L, BP 150/96 mmHg, pulse 81 bpm, weight 71 kg. His hands feel cool and there is no tremor. The chest is clear, heart sounds are normal, and there is no ankle swelling. Assessment: Hypothyroidism. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to keep a regular sleep routine and eat a balanced diet. Follow-up in 6 weeks with a repeat TSH.

Visit note | 2025-01-06 12:00 PM | Dr. Fahmida Yasmin, ENT | Patient: Nayeem Hossain, 34, male. Mr. Hossain attends with a throat that has been sore for three days, and he says swallowing has become painful enough that he has been avoiding solid food. He also reports fever with chills, especially at night. He drives a bus on the Savar route and mentions that the symptoms began soon after he drank cold beverages at a wedding he attended in Savar. He has no long-term illnesses. He denies earache, cough, and difficulty breathing. On examination: temperature 102.5°F, BP 131/81 mmHg, pulse 109 bpm, weight 64 kg. Both tonsils are enlarged, red, and covered with a few white spots, and the throat is generally inflamed. The neck is supple with no swelling. Assessment: Acute tonsillitis. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to gargle with warm salt water, eat soft food, and drink plenty of fluids. Follow-up in 1 week.
